title: Imagery Rescripting and Reprocessing Therapy in Suicide Bereavement
summary:
The suicide of a close person represents a particularly distressing form of loss and is often associated with complex, intense, and long-term psychological consequences for the bereaved (Levi-Belz et al., 2023). In Germany, psychosocial care for suicide survivors is predominantly provided through self-help groups (e.g., Angehörige um Suizid AGUS e.V.). Specific and effective treatment options are largely lacking. A systematic review examining the efficacy of interventions for suicide survivors found only insufficient effectiveness across the included studies (Linde et al., 2017). The interventions led to only minor improvements in grief-related symptoms. It is therefore urgently necessary to develop and evaluate targeted treatment approaches.

In particular, Imagery Rescripting and Reprocessing Therapy (IRRT) appears to be a promising approach in the treatment of bereaved individuals. IRRT is a transdiagnostic method originally developed for the treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and is now increasingly applied to other disorders as well (Morina et al., 2017; Schaitz et al., 2020; Schmucker & Köster, 2016). Within IRRT treatment, negative events and images are modified through guided imagery. Memories can thus be reprocessed and adapted from the perspective of the affected person in the present.

For this reason, the present study aims to treat individuals bereaved by suicide within the framework of a short-term psychotherapeutic intervention using IRRT.
conditions: Prolonged Grief. PTSD, cPTSD, depression, suicidal ideation

interventions.name:
Participants in the intervention group receive the intervention based on IRRT after a baseline phase. The intervention takes place in an outpatient setting and is conducted by psychological psychotherapists specialized in cognitive behavioral therapy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Loss of a close person due to suicide, loss occurred ≥ 6 months ago, fluency in German,Informed consent to participate in the study, TGI-SR+ score ≥ 60
Exclusion criteria:
acute suicidality, schizophrenia, acute psychosis, current psychotherapeutic treatment
